vulnerabilities.message: Hardcoded AWS access key detected: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
vulnerabilities.description: AWS access keys should never be hardcoded in source code as they provide access to cloud resources.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use AWS IAM roles, environment variables, or AWS Secrets Manager for credential management.

vulnerabilities.message: Hardcoded AWS secret key detected: wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
vulnerabilities.description: AWS secret keys provide full access to AWS resources and should never be hardcoded.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use AWS IAM roles, environment variables, or AWS Secrets Manager for credential management.

vulnerabilities.description: Live Stripe API keys should never be hardcoded as they can process real payments.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use environment variables or Stripe's webhook authentication for secure API key management.

vulnerabilities.message: Hardcoded database URL with credentials detected
vulnerabilities.description: Database connection strings with credentials should not be hardcoded in source code.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use environment variables or a secure configuration management system for database credentials.

vulnerabilities.description: Email addresses should not be hardcoded in source code as they can be used for phishing attacks.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use configuration files or environment variables for email addresses.

vulnerabilities.description: Phone numbers should not be hardcoded in source code as they can be used for social engineering attacks.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use configuration files or environment variables for phone numbers.

vulnerabilities.description: Credit card numbers should never be hardcoded in source code as they are highly sensitive payment data.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credit card numbers and use tokenization for payment processing.

vulnerabilities.message: Logging sensitive payment data (credit card number)
vulnerabilities.description: Logging credit card numbers violates PCI DSS requirements and can lead to data breaches.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove credit card logging or mask all but the last 4 digits.

vulnerabilities.description: CVV codes should never be logged as they are highly sensitive payment verification data.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove CVV logging entirely. CVV should only be used for verification and never stored or logged.

vulnerabilities.message: Saving sensitive transaction data to unencrypted file
vulnerabilities.description: Writing payment data to unencrypted files violates PCI DSS requirements and creates a security risk.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Encrypt all payment data files or use a secure database with encryption at rest.

vulnerabilities.message: Sending sensitive data over HTTP instead of HTTPS
vulnerabilities.description: Payment data should always be transmitted over encrypted HTTPS connections.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use HTTPS for all payment-related API calls and verify SSL certificate validation.

vulnerabilities.message: Potential SQL injection vulnerability in query construction
vulnerabilities.description: String formatting in SQL queries can lead to SQL injection attacks.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or an ORM to prevent SQL injection.
vulnerabilities.match: query = f"SELECT * FROM transactions WHERE customer_email = '{customer_email}'"

vulnerabilities.message: Logging full credit card number during validation
vulnerabilities.description: Credit card numbers should not be logged during validation processes.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Log only masked credit card numbers (e.g., ****-****-****-1234) or avoid logging entirely.

vulnerabilities.message: Storing credit card in memory without encryption
vulnerabilities.description: Credit card data should be encrypted when stored in memory to prevent memory dumps from exposing sensitive data.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use secure memory management or avoid storing credit card data in memory.

vulnerabilities.message: Global variable containing sensitive customer data
vulnerabilities.description: Global variables with sensitive data can be accessed by any part of the application.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use proper data structures with access controls or encrypt sensitive data in global variables.

complianceViolations: PCI DSS Requirement 3 - Protect stored cardholder data

PCI DSS Requirement 7 - Restrict access to cardholder data

recommendations: Immediately remove all hardcoded AWS and Stripe credentials
Implement proper secrets management using environment variables or cloud-native services
Remove all credit card logging and implement PCI DSS compliant logging
Use HTTPS for all payment-related communications
Implement proper encryption for all payment data storage
Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
Implement secure memory management for sensitive data
Remove hardcoded PII and use secure configuration management
Conduct a PCI DSS compliance audit
